The universal animosity to DLC is getting kind of annoying at this point.

In my opinion, there are a couple of things to consider here. First, DLC isn't going to go away, no matter how hard people wish for that, for whatever reason. It's also not a new phenomenon, expansion packs have been a common thing for games even in the 90s (and in some cases even before that). Also, not all DLC is created equal. Yes, there is outrageous stuff like Mafia 2 and its DLC, and it's fair and well to critizise that, but there is also DLC like the ones for FO3 / NV or like Borderlands, which in my opinion is DLC done right, i.e. more and new content added after the base game's release that don't diminish the base game's value because they are clearly things the original story depends on that were just cut out to be sold for a markup at a later point, like with Mafia 2. Condemning all DLC across the board is just stupid when there are clearly different kinds and example where DLC can be done right (though that is obviously a subjective distinction).

Second, announcing or planning DLC before a base game is even released is also a reality that's not necessarily an unethical or cash-grabbing thing, it's just a consequence of how game development, especially for AAA games works these days. The way these projects are planned and executed necessitates hard dates with content locks, beyond which date no more content can be added in order for testing, finalization and sending the gold versions off to the presses (or digital distributors) to happen. Software development isn't as trivial as a lot of people imagine it to be, meeting deadlines can be a massive pain in the ass and these problems grow as the project gets bigger. AAA games with often hundreds of people involved in their production are a logistical nightmare as proven by the constant postponing of release dates we are all used to, and the people involved certainly don't keep pushing their product's release dates ahead all the time just for the fun of it. So with deadlines and content locks in place, some part of the developers can start working on DLC while others are testing and finalizing the product for the base game's release and I don't see anything inherently wrong or unethical about that. This is, of course, provided a publisher will even fund this practice. Which is why you don't see this with all games, but with games like FO4 where financial success is pretty much guaranteed, it makes absolutely sense to do this. The alternative would be for the publisher to cut funding and the dev studio to lay off the people after the base game's development is finished. Then, maybe, if the game ends up successful, they can start hiring more devs to start working on DLC and get a massive delay between DLC release and the base game's release, if it is greenlit at all.

And finally, pre-orders, as much as we hate them (and rightfully so, in my opinion) are also here to stay because, like it or not, they make money and make sense from a business perspective. They make up a huge amount of the profit gained from a game, they give estimations to the general sales of a game before the product is even released, and big companies and their shareholders love that kind of stuff so it's not going away (unless people stop supporting the practice, but good luck with that). It's also the least objectionable thing to me because it personally doesn't affect me at all. I just don't pre-order, period, and beyond that it's none of my concern. And again back to FO4, thee Fallout games have traditionally offered GOTY editions with all the DLC included for quite reasonable prices like two years down the road, so if you absolutely don't want to support these practices you can just wait and get a great deal. You don't have to buy the DLC seasons pass now, you can wait until the DLC is released, watch gameplay videos on youtube and read reviews and ask friends and judge for yourself whether it's worth buying or not. But again, I don't really see anything inherently reprehensible about this.

As long as the game ends up being good and the devs release more content for that good game, I'm all for it, whether they're starting out to plan and develop that content before the base game is even released doesn't make a difference to me.
